entry.title: Show HN: PeerTalk.ai - Let your agent talk to a friend's agent (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Little experiment I've been cooking up. I often find myself wanting to do one of the following: - Get my agent and a someone else's agent to agree on something, after we've been discussing the same topic in different threads - Give someone temporary access to talk to one of my agents for a specific purpose, to help them do something or help them understand something - Ask a co-worker for access to chat with their agent, to understand something it has been working on without it having to dump out its entire context into a shared doc - Give two different agents working for me the ability to quickly chat to resolve something when they have overlapping concerns So I built https://peertalk.ai to let agents talk to each other over WebRTC. Obviously only use this if you fully trust the other person. There are lots of safeguards, but this is essentially inviting prompt injection if it's not someone you trust completely -- or an agent fully under your control. Hope people find this helpful! Pretty early days so very open to your feedback and ideas. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49862920 Points: 3 # Comments: 3

entry.title: Show HN: All/Some - A free logic puzzle game about set relationships (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: All/Some is a web app where you work out how sets relate using "all," "some," and "none" relationships. My husband and I made the game together. I create the puzzles and he does the code and design. The idea came from a puzzle I posted on Instagram (@critikid) that went viral. In the puzzle, people had to match groups of words to the correct Euler diagrams. People liked it so much that we decided to turn it into a full game. All/Some offers a free daily challenge (ad free), and there are more puzzles for members. There are also thematic collections for members on topics like biology and history, and I'm working on adding more. We would like feedback on whether you'd like to see variations to the puzzle format. We're considering skipping the easier first 2 steps a puzzle or giving players more than 4 answer choices. I'd also like to hear thoughts on the paid membership and its pricing. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49862912 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Reladraw - A diagram language where you decide where to place things (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I love making diagrams to help understand, plan, etc. However, the options are (A) auto-placement languages like Mermaid or Graphviz (which don't let me decide how the diagram looks), or (B) software like Draw.io which are powerful but are very time consuming (and inefficient for agents to manipulate). I wanted to have the benefits of both, where you can define a diagram in a diagram language, but also retain a high degree of control over what the diagram looks like. I also wanted this to work well for humans and agents. On the Github link, there's a playground where you can try it out without installation. There's also instructions for a simple npm install and for installing a skill you can use with Claude or other agents. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49858513 Points: 212 # Comments: 60

entry.title: Turning GLM-5.3-Flash into a Jev-like decision model (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: We found an approach to get Jev-like properties from standard LLMs like GLM-5.3-Flash. The core idea is to craft the input prompt so that the first output token answers the question. This makes it possible to get a decision with a single forward pass. In the blog post, we describe the approach in detail for GLM-5.3-Flash and vLLM. We benchmark this setup against Jev and Laya. We find that our setup is on-par with Jev in terms of accuracy and speed and that it substantially outperforms Laya. Still, in terms of costs per decision, Jev is several x better than our setup. In turn, our setup supports vision inputs. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49857656 Points: 45 # Comments: 25
